instruction: I've drafted an e-mail reminder. Please add the e-mail addresses of students who haven't paid to the receiver field, and add the e-mail addresses of students whose names start with 'K', 'L', or 'M' to the CC field using the payment record.

metadata.explanation: Task requires two separate operations: (1) Finding students who haven't paid (Payment='No') and adding to To field, (2) Finding students whose names start with K, L, or M and adding to CC field. Verified with Python: Unpaid students are Fox, Iron, Nancy, Stella. Students with names starting with K/L/M are Kathy, Lily, Mike. Expected To field: fox@someuniversity.edu, iron@someuniversity.edu, nancy@someuniversity.edu, stella@someuniversity.edu. Expected CC field: kathy@someuniversity.edu, lily@someuniversity.edu, mike@someuniversity.edu. Uses existing check_accessibility_tree metric to verify all seven emails are present in their respective fields.
metadata.scoring_breakdown: All-or-nothing: 1.0 if all four unpaid student emails are in To field AND all three K/L/M student emails are in CC field, 0.0 otherwise

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator correctly verifies both requirements: unpaid students in To field and K/L/M students in CC field
All seven required email addresses are checked with appropriate CSS selectors
Selectors correctly distinguish between To field (4 emails) and CC field (3 emails) using label[name=To] and label[name=Cc]
Using name*= (contains) operator is appropriate for matching email addresses within pill labels
Expected values (fox@, iron@, nancy@, stella@ for To; kathy@, lily@, mike@ for CC) match the data analysis in metadata
check_accessibility_tree metric returns 0.0 if any selector fails, correctly implementing all-or-nothing scoring

Complete coverage: both instruction requirements (unpaid students + K/L/M names) are fully verified
